task: Ground factual claims for the human-process automation platform purpose work.
output_summary: Added a durable platform purpose rule that the workspace exists to reduce repetitive human work and elapsed time by modeling real human processes into small reusable automation assets.

evidence.reliability: Tracked web-first record with queries, checked sources, ignored weak sources, plan impact, and uncertainty.
Tracked requirement baseline and spec artifacts for REQ-WS-045.
Tracked operating documents that expose the human-process automation purpose.
Durable instructions and memory bootstrap anchors updated and validated by config/memory checks.
Official Google SRE book chapter checked for toil definition and time-allocation rationale.
Official Google SRE workbook chapter checked for identifying, quantifying, and reducing toil.
IBM Research publication summary checked for human web-task repetition and task-model generation.
IBM official explainer checked for RPA as repetitive task automation that emulates human processes.
Microsoft Learn documentation checked for process/task mining, bottleneck discovery, and automation opportunity discovery.
JSON syntax, config contract, memory bootstrap, docs audit, naming audit, structure audit, workspace index, task board, workspace health, and work timer checks passed after regenerating stale maps.

claims.statement: The repository now has REQ-WS-045 defining the platform's purpose as reducing repetitive human work and elapsed time through human-process modeling and automation-worthy asset promotion.
verification_steps: Read the requirements baseline and the human-process automation spec.

claims.statement: The philosophy, platform identity, README, and capability governance documents now express that automation is a means to reduce repetition and time, not an end in itself.
verification_steps: Read the operating documents listed in evidence.

claims.statement: Persistent instructions, AGENTS, and memory bootstrap now include the human-process automation purpose and boundaries.
verification_steps: Read the instruction files and run memory/config checks.

claims.statement: Google SRE materials define toil as repetitive, automatable manual work and frame toil reduction as a way to preserve time for engineering work.
verification_steps: Checked Google SRE book and workbook pages and captured plan impact in the web search record.

claims.statement: IBM LiveAction research supports the idea that real user activity can reveal repeated web behaviors that can be modeled for automation.
verification_steps: Checked IBM Research publication summary and captured plan impact in the web search record.

claims.statement: IBM RPA and Microsoft process/task mining materials support using human process models and task/process observations to identify automation opportunities.
verification_steps: Checked IBM and Microsoft official materials and captured plan impact in the web search record.

claims.statement: Automation should preserve human judgment, validation criteria, and rollback boundaries.
verification_steps: Checked that the boundary is recorded as a repository operating rule and not as an external universal claim.

uncertainty_notes: The actual time saved by future automation depends on repeated measurements in work timing records and evaluator outcomes.
Human-process observation must remain bounded by privacy, permission, and the user-provided task context.
limitation_notes: This change updates platform philosophy, requirements, rules, and memory anchors. It does not implement a new automation runtime.
The policy intentionally avoids claiming that every repeated task should be automated.
